report:
## Yes — regular CT screening reduces lung-cancer deaths in heavy (ex-)smokers

**Evidence base:**

1. **National Lung Screening Trial (NLST, 2011, NEJM)** — the largest US randomized trial, enrolled >53,000 current/former heavy smokers (≥30 pack-years, quit ≤15 yrs). Three annual low-dose CT (LDCT) screens reduced lung-cancer mortality by **20%** relative to chest X-ray, and reduced all-cause mortality by ~6–7% (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1102873).

2. **NELSON trial (2020, NEJM)** — the largest European randomized trial (Netherlands/Belgium), using volumetric CT with less-frequent, decreasing-interval screening in high-risk smokers. It confirmed a mortality benefit, with lung-cancer mortality significantly lower in the screened group (rate ratio ~0.75 combining men and women; NNS ≈130 over 10 years to prevent one death) (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1911793).

3. **Systematic reviews/meta-analyses** of these and smaller trials confirm a consistent, statistically significant reduction in lung-cancer-specific mortality among heavy smokers screened with LDCT, though without a demonstrated reduction in all-cause mortality overall (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11718421/; https://di.aerzteblatt.de/int/archive/article/231736).

4. Based on this evidence, the **US Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF)** recommends annual LDCT screening for adults 50–80 years old with a ≥20 pack-year smoking history who currently smoke or quit within 15 years (https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/lung-cancer-screening).

**Caveats:** Benefits must be weighed against harms — false positives, unnecessary invasive follow-up, overdiagnosis, and cumulative radiation exposure — but net benefit favors screening in this high-risk group.

**Conclusion:** Multiple large randomized controlled trials (NLST, NELSON) and subsequent meta-analyses provide strong, consistent evidence that regular LDCT screening reduces lung-cancer mortality in heavy current/former smokers, supporting current major screening guidelines.
